title: Probe Curation Stewardship and Annotation Charter
author: Aisha N. Patel
content:
Summary

Purpose: Define a repeatable, cross-team charter for curating, labeling, and stewarding probe sets (prompt probes and short synthetic interactions) that feed the eval-harness, regression triage tooling, and quantization-sensitivity suites. This document standardizes probe metadata, acceptance criteria, annotation contracts, and the rollout checklist for new probe bundles.

Scope
- Applies to probes intended for: production regression detection, quantization sensitivity, KV-cache stability tests, multi-turn coherence checks, and privacy/PII stress probes.
- Includes both synthetic probes (generated by internal seeders) and real-world-sampled probe candidates that enter the probe-store.
- Does not cover long-running offline benchmarks (>1M tokens) which are managed by the benchmarking-and-perf-suite team.

Definitions
- Probe: a single test request (prompt + optional context + expected behavioral signals) used by eval tooling.
- Probe Bundle: a versioned collection of probes with a manifest, metadata, and annotation state.
- Steward: owner responsible for the probe bundle lifecycle (curation, triage, retirement).

Roles and Responsibilities
1) Probe Steward (Primary): typically applied-ml engineer or product analyst. Responsibilities:
   - Define objectives and coverage matrix for the bundle (e.g., long-context coherence, entity hallucination).
   - Approve acceptance criteria and promotion readiness.
   - Own related JIRA/retro tickets and schedule canary evals.
2) Annotation Lead: manages labeler workforce and QA.
   - Produces annotation guide, trains annotators, runs adjudication.
3) Evaluator/CI Owner: integrates the bundle into eval-harness and sets runtime params.
4) Regression Oncall Contact: triages alerts generated by probes in production shadow pipelines.

Probe Manifest Schema (required fields)
- id: unique probe id (UUID)
- bundle_version: semver (e.g., 1.3.0)
- intent_tag: short string (e.g., refund-flow, multi-turn-summarize)
- slice_tags: list of strings (e.g., ["long_context", "numeric_answer"])
- sensitive_flag: yes|no|pii_masked
- expected_behaviors: list of behavior checks (e.g., ["correct_entity", "no-invented-dates"])
- ttl_days: integer (retirement after X days unless renewed)
- provenance: one of ["user-sampled", "synthetic-seeder", "partner-contrib"]
- annotation_state: draft|annotated|adjudicated|frozen
- annotation_version: semver
- steward: person/email
- created_at, last_updated (ISO dates)

Example JSON snippet (manifest):
{
  "id": "probe-8f4c2a6e",
  "bundle_version": "0.1.0",
  "intent_tag": "invoice-summary",
  "slice_tags": ["multistep", "financial"],
  "sensitive_flag": "pii_masked",
  "expected_behaviors": ["preserve-numeric-entities", "concise-summary"],
  "ttl_days": "365",
  "provenance": "user-sampled",
  "annotation_state": "annotated",
  "annotation_version": "1.0.0",
  "steward": "aisha.patel@redwood.ai",
  "created_at": "2025-11-14",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-03"
}

Acceptance Criteria and Quality Gates
- Coverage: every high-priority product intent (as defined in the coverage matrix) must have at least N=120 probes distributed across slices unless otherwise approved.
- Annotation quality: adjudicated inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff alpha or Cohen kappa) >= 0.80 for binary labels; >= 0.75 for multi-class.
- Stability probes: for each bundle, include 20% of probes marked as "stability" which exercise KV cache boundary conditions and quantized inference (see Quant Flagging below).
- Sensitivity tagging: probes that changed label under quantized runs or mixed-precision runs must be flagged with quant_susceptible=true.
- Regression detectability: historically validated bundles should map to at least 3 regression alert signatures when run against two different model variants.

Annotation Contract and Guide (short version)
1) Annotator tasks are atomic: each task contains a single probe and at most three micro-labels (correctness, hallucination, harmfulness).
2) Label definitions must include 3 canonical examples per label (positive/negative/edge-case).
3) Adjudication: any probe with >=25% disagreement moves to adjudication queue; adjudicator must provide a 1-3 sentence rationale.
4) Annotator throughput and QA: monthly spot-checks: 200 probes sampled per annotator; acceptable error rate <4%.

Probe Priority Scoring (curation heuristic)
- Score components (normalized 0-1): novelty(0.25), user-impact(0.35), regression-signal-history(0.2), coverage-gap(0.2).
- Priority = weighted sum; bundles with Priority >= 0.7 advance to canary eval stage.

Integration with Eval Harness and CI
- Bundle registration: use CLI `probectl register --manifest bundle.json` to publish to probe-store and tag for eval-harness.
- Canary policy: default canary runs: 3 seeds, two model variants (current-prod, candidate), runtime budget 1200 tokens per probe, sample 200 probes (top-priority subset).
- Runtime SLOs: smoke-eval < 2 hours, full-bundle-run < 24 hours (for bundles <5k probes). If runtime exceeds SLO by 25%, evaluator owner must be paged and a performance triage ticket opened.

Quantization and Hardware Sensitivity Flags
- Each probe must set quant_flag: one of [none, quant-8bit, quant-4bit] if it is intended for quant-sensitivity suites.
- For probes with quant_flag != none, Evaluator must run both FP16 and specified quant modes and produce a per-probe delta metric: response-change-score (0-1). Probes with delta >= 0.25 are `quant_susceptible` and must be included in follow-up diagnosis.

Regression Triage Fast-Path (procedure)
1) Alert fires from runtime monitoring: probe_failure_rate > threshold (default 5%) OR Response Stability Index delta > 0.05 over 1 day.
2) Triage steps (fast-path):
   a) Steward validates probe manifest and runs targeted shadow-run (single-variant replay) using `probectl replay --ids <list> --model current-prod`.
   b) If failure reproducible, annotate failure type (semantic drift, tokenization, quantization, runtime-eviction) and escalate to owner team.
   c) If not reproducible, expand scope to ensemble runs and collect traces (kv-cache logs, seed RNG, exact token stream).
3) Postmortem requirement: incidents with customer-visible impact must produce a 72-hour interim note and a 2-week formal RCA with mitigation plan.

Retention and Retirement Policy
- Active bundles: retain full annotation state and provenance for 540 days.
- Archive: after TTL expiration or steward retirement, move to cold-store (metadata retained) and mark public queryable but excluded from automated CI unless explicitly reactivated.

Metrics and Dashboards (concrete list)
- Probe health dashboard (prod): probe_failure_rate, mean_response_time, median_response_stability_index, quant_susceptible_count.
- Eval-harness job metrics: job_latency_p50/p95, tokens_consumed, and per-bundle success_rate.
- Annotation QA: per-annotator agreement, adjudication backlog, labeling throughput.

Rollout Checklist for New Probe Bundle
1) Produce coverage matrix and steward assignment.
2) Draft annotation guide and seed 50 probes for pilot labeling.
3) Run pilot: achieve kappa >= 0.8 or iterate guide.
4) Register bundle and run canary eval.
5) Promote to scheduled nightly-run if canary stable for 3 consecutive runs.
6) Add to regression watchlist and enable alerting thresholds.

References and Links
- Eval harness: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-harness-core
- Probe CLI: internal repo: git@redwood:tools/probectl
- Quantization playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-impact-synthesis-for-prompt-families-2026

Appendix: Quick commands
- Register bundle: probectl register --manifest bundle.json --owner aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- Run canary: probectl run --bundle probe-bundle@0.1.0 --targets candidate,current-prod --seeds 3 --sample 200
- Replay probe list: probectl replay --ids probe-*,probe-* --model candidate --trace kvcache,tokenstream

Document maintenance: The steward must schedule a quarterly review (every 90 days) to refresh coverage and retire stale probes.
